entries.title: A cleaner support dashboard, and replies that actually teach
entries.preview: Behind the scenes: a compact, colour-coded support queue, and missing email bodies can no longer hide a lesson.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes release about the Saka team's support tools. The support queue is now easier to scan: each ticket keeps its conversation and investigation notes folded away until needed, urgent tickets stand out in red, in-progress ones in amber and new ones in blue, and forwarded subject lines are cleaned up. We also traced a real case where a support answer arrived without its body - the reply reached us but the text was missing, so nothing could be learned from it. That can no longer happen silently: any missing or empty email body is now recorded for the team, and every human answer is tagged with whether its text arrived. Nothing about your own WhatsApp conversations, records, reports, reminders or billing changes.

entries.title: Support replies now update the ticket and show in the thread
entries.preview: When our team replies, the ticket now moves to In progress and the conversation appears in the dashboard thread.
entries.summary: A support-tool fix from a real test. When the Saka team replied to an escalated support ticket, the reply email reached the customer - but the ticket's status silently stayed Escalated, the dashboard's In progress counter stayed at zero, and the reply did not appear in the dashboard thread, so it looked like nothing had happened. Two hidden causes were fixed: a very old database rule was rejecting the In progress and Resolved statuses, and the ticket lookup could mistake a one-off network hiccup for 'ticket not found'. Now every reply moves the ticket to In progress, the dashboard shows the full conversation - your message, our reply and internal notes - and any future status problem is reported honestly instead of being silently swallowed. Nothing about your own WhatsApp conversations, records, reports, reminders or billing changes.

entries.title: Behind the scenes: safer local testing for support
entries.preview: A behind-the-scenes reliability release for our support agent - nothing changes in your app.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes reliability release. While preparing the support agent that answers emails to support@reports.sakafleet.com, we found that a developer's local setting could quietly change how one of our automated checks behaved. It is fixed: the check now sets its own switch, proves it, and restores it afterwards, so a test run can never be influenced by a leftover local setting. Nothing about your conversations, records, reports, reminders or billing changes.

entries.title: A signup door right where you sign in
entries.preview: Landed on the login page without an account? A new 'Start your free trial' link takes you straight to sign up.
entries.summary: A small navigation fix. The dashboard sign-in page now ends with a friendly line - "Don't have an account yet? Start your free trial" - linking to the Saka Fleet website so a first-time visitor who landed there by mistake can begin signup in one click. The superadmin sign-in door is unchanged and never shows it. Nothing about signing in, sessions, trials or your data changes.

entries.title: A signup that always finishes
entries.preview: Returning to finish an unverified signup now re-sends your code and opens the code screen - no more dead ends.
entries.summary: A fix from a real visitor. Someone who started a signup earlier - the account existed but the email was never confirmed - came back to finish it, and the form quietly stopped: the page said nothing, and the email that promised a new code never sent one. Now a returning, unconfirmed signup is recognised properly: the same account is kept (your number and plan are never changed), a fresh verification code is sent to your email, and the site opens the code screen straight away. If the Continue button is still busy checking your details when you hit Enter, the page now tells you it is checking instead of doing nothing - and any refusal now explains itself in plain words.

entries.title: A single, careful place for the team to look after accounts
entries.preview: Behind the scenes: the Saka team now has one audited console for every account, with typed confirmations.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes release about how the Saka team looks after accounts. Support now works from one console that shows every profile - owners, drivers and brand-new sign-ups - with its plan or trial status and vehicle count. From there the team can correct a name, email, country or units, extend a trial, apply a plan after an offline payment (the billing history gains a clearly marked manual line), confirm an email when it has been proven another way, leave an internal note, end stray dashboard sessions, and - only with a typed WIPE and a recorded reason - erase an account. Every one of those actions requires the word typed exactly, records why it was done, and keeps an audit trail; the superadmin's own account can never be edited, impersonated or wiped. Your records, reports and reminders are untouched.

entries.title: Site analytics now arrive by a first-party address
entries.preview: Google Tag Manager now loads from our own gtm.sakafleet.com address, so consented measurement survives ad blockers.
entries.summary: A small, invisible privacy-respecting change to the website. If you choose "Analytics & marketing", the measurement script now loads from our own gtm.sakafleet.com address instead of the standard Google address - the same Google Tag Manager container, delivered first-party, so the measurement you consented to is far less likely to be blocked. Nothing changes about what we collect: the script still loads only after your explicit opt-in, rejecting non-essential cookies still loads nothing at all, and your WhatsApp records, reports and reminders are untouched.

entries.title: The cookie bar you can always see and tap
entries.preview: On a phone, the cookie choice now sits above everything - clearly visible, above the home indicator, and easy to tap.
entries.summary: A mobile fix from a real visitor. The cookie bar was rendered underneath the signup window, so on some phones it looked invisible even though the form was asking for a cookie choice - and the very bottom of the screen can hide behind the iPhone home indicator. The bar now floats above every window the site opens, sits safely above the bottom edge of the screen, wraps its message and buttons onto their own rows on small phones with bigger tap targets, and gently pulses when the signup form needs your choice. The form now shows a short line pointing at the bar instead of a pop-up alert, so the next step is always obvious.

entries.title: Finished signups, and a plate you can send later
entries.preview: Already signed up? Jump straight to Saka on WhatsApp - and save your car registration even without the plate.
entries.summary: Two small fixes from real visitors. If someone tries to sign up with a number or email that already has a Saka account, the form used to leave them at a dead end with a greyed-out button. Now an account that still needs its email verified can simply continue and the code is re-sent, and an already-verified account sees a direct button to chat with Saka on WhatsApp. Separately, registering a car used to wait on the number plate: if the plate wasn't nearby, the conversation just stopped. Now reply 'no plate yet' (or 'later', or say the logbook isn't with you) and Saka saves your draft with everything already shared - send the plate, or a photo of the logbook, whenever you're ready and the registration finishes. Nothing is registered and no trial starts until the plate arrives, and nothing is ever deleted.

entries.title: Signup measurement, with your consent
entries.preview: With your consent, signup now sends Google a hashed email and phone so we can see which ads bring people here.
entries.summary: A small website update about measurement. When someone signs up, the site can now tell Google Ads and Google Analytics that a signup happened - and, only if you opted in to analytics, include the email address and phone number you entered so the measurement is accurate. Those details are hashed with SHA-256 before they ever travel, are never shared when you choose "Reject non-essential", and nothing about your WhatsApp records, reports or reminders changes. Because what we measure has changed, the cookie banner asks everyone for a fresh choice.

entries.title: Receipt photos are evidence, never paperwork
entries.preview: A fuel receipt photo now links to the exact expense it confirms - even when you send it halfway through logging.
entries.summary: A real-conversation fix. If you opened a fuel entry, then sent the receipt photo while Saka was still asking the amount, the photo was read correctly but filed as a vehicle registration certificate instead of a receipt: the expense saved without its receipt and the records page showed a dash where the photo should be. Now a receipt is always recognised as a receipt - the photo links to the exact entry it confirms, the total is read from the cash line (never from a tax-rate number), and a receipt can never replace the real logbook in your documents. The driver's vehicle files were repaired too.

entries.title: Every account is accounted for
entries.preview: The team's morning numbers now show how many accounts have a vehicle and how many are still finding their wheels.
entries.summary: A small clarity fix behind the scenes. The team's daily briefing used to say how many profiles were registered and then name only the ones with vehicles, which left the rest looking unexplained. It now says it plainly: how many accounts have a vehicle and how many do not yet - so support can spot someone who signed up but never added a car and reach out. Your own records, reports and reminders are untouched.

entries.title: The test tools finish the job
entries.preview: Testing all templates now continues where it stopped, and a tapped button behaves like a tap for everyone.
entries.summary: A quiet operator-only patch from the first live run of the template tools. Testing all messages used to stop after the first five and start over every time - it now remembers where it stopped for an hour, so simply repeating the command walks the whole list, retrying anything that was refused. A button tapped from the operator's own phone used to be answered as an unknown admin command; now it opens the same flow it would for a customer. And the button audit can look at the phone the test was sent to, not only the operator's own, naming that number with only its last four digits. Customers see no change.

entries.title: Receipts are read, not searched
entries.preview: Send a fuel receipt photo and Saka reads it — total, litres and odometer — instead of answering it like a search.
entries.summary: A follow-up from a real conversation. Sending a fuel receipt photo could come back with a line that looked like a search result instead of a reading, and a second copy of the same receipt could start nothing at all. Now a receipt photo always opens the confirmation card: Saka shows the total, the litres and the odometer it read, and nothing is saved until you say yes. A few smaller money fixes ride along: a parking amount can no longer be inflated by the dates in your sentence (300 for the 7th, 8th and 9th stays 300), and a fuel price per litre can never be saved as the amount you spent. Asking to delete a compliance date no longer risks touching your expenses — compliance dates are corrected, not deleted. And 'cancel transfer' now answers honestly instead of starting a new handover.

entries.title: Test the messages on any phone
entries.preview: Send a test template to a chosen phone number, not just the operator's own, with the same safety caps.
entries.summary: A small operator-only patch. The template test command now accepts an optional phone number, so the team can check a message on a regular device instead of only the operator's own phone - for example a local number ending 52529 is understood automatically, while other countries are typed with their full code. Nothing is ever sent to a malformed number: the reply says so plainly. The five-sends-every-ten-minutes guard now counts against the operator rather than the receiving phone, so switching devices can never raise the limit, and the audit trail keeps only the last four digits of whoever received the test. Nothing changes for customers.

entries.title: Test the messages, prove the buttons
entries.preview: Fire a real approved template to the operator's phone, and prove every reply button reaches a live flow.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes release for the team. The superadmin can now send any approved WhatsApp message template to their own number with one command, so they can see exactly what customers receive before it matters - one message at a time or the whole list in a paced run, capped at five sends every ten minutes. Each send reports honestly what happened: accepted with a message id, rejected by Meta, blocked, or not configured yet (naming the template the operator still needs to approve). A second command audits every reply button on every template: it lists what the templates declare, what each button title maps to, and any recent taps, and it flags a tap that has nowhere to go. The audit also records one known gap - the 'Log Fuel' button still relies on Saka's language understanding rather than a fixed shortcut - so it can never be forgotten. Nothing changes for customers: no new messages are sent to them.

entries.title: One tap from the re-engage message
entries.preview: Four one-tap buttons on the re-engage message: log fuel, set a reminder, log an expense, or open your dashboard.
entries.summary: A small follow-up to the final release. When Saka reaches out after two quiet weeks, the approved message now carries four buttons - Log Fuel, Set Reminder, Log Expense and Dashboard - so replying takes one tap instead of typing. Each tap goes through the exact same path as the typed phrase: it opens the fuel or expense quiz, starts a reminder, or hands over your dashboard sign-in link. The feature tip template stays as a plain message. Both message families remain switched off until the team enables them, and nothing changes for anyone before then.

entries.title: A menu on every screen, your own lanes, and gentle tips
entries.preview: A clean dashboard menu, owner/driver lane switching, and one gentle feature tip after activation.
entries.summary: This is the final release of the program, and it polishes three everyday things. The dashboard now has one tidy menu: on wide screens the same row of links stays, and on phones and tablets a menu button opens a full-screen list built from exactly the same links - nothing hidden, nothing duplicated - while the yellow impersonation banner always stays visible above it. Second: if you both own a vehicle and drive one, the dashboard now shows an Owner / Driver switch at the top. It moves between your two dashboards through the same checks as signing in (an owner needs a live trial or paid plan, a driver needs a live vehicle assignment), and if you drive more than one vehicle you also get a small vehicle picker. While a superadmin is viewing an account read-only the switch is hidden. Third: after your trial activates, Saka can send one short tip about a feature you have not tried yet - your web dashboard, one-line expense logging, voice notes, reports or compliance photos - and at most one friendly follow-up two days later, only if you still have not tried it. Silence re-engagement can now also reach you through an approved template if you have been away for two weeks. Both of these message families ship switched off: nothing new is sent until the team turns them on, and until then nothing changes at all.

entries.title: A sharper website, one switch for monthly or annual
entries.preview: A calmer header on every screen, one billing switch for monthly or annual, and a clearer launch offer.
entries.summary: This release polishes the website from top to bottom. The header now has one pattern instead of two: below wide desktop it becomes a tidy menu button, and the logo is the same size everywhere - on the smallest phones it switches to the square mark so nothing is ever squeezed. The launch banner keeps its live slot count with the approved copy, stays stuck to the top while you scroll, and the menu now opens below it instead of hiding behind it. Pricing gains one simple switch: monthly or annual, with annual showing the full yearly figure and the 30 percent saving. Your choice is remembered on your next visit, and local currencies still work exactly as before. Every mention of paying by card has been rewritten to the plainer no payment, and the footer now carries a Support link. On the dashboard, the logo now takes you where it should: the public site when you are signed out, your own overview when you are signed in, and the same owner overview while a superadmin is impersonating (only Exit leaves it).

entries.title: Phone-friendly PDFs and smarter expense checks
entries.preview: Reports now arrive phone-shaped, logbook photos are kept, and impossible expenses are gently refused.
entries.summary: Four polish fixes in one release. First: every report link Saka sends on WhatsApp now opens a phone-shaped PDF (A5, nothing smaller than 10 point type), while your dashboard offers both the phone layout and the classic A4 download - and the reports page has a button for each. Second: during registration Saka now invites you to send your logbook photo and keeps it with the vehicle for safekeeping; on the Free plan the details are kept and Saka says so honestly. Third: if you send a logbook before the vehicle is registered, the photo is no longer lost - it is held and filed under the new vehicle the moment registration completes. Fourth: an expense that cannot exist on an asset is now refused with a helpful suggestion - tyres on a generator, or mooring fees on a car - instead of being saved where it would quietly spoil your reports. "Other" is always available for the genuinely unusual spend.

entries.title: The Reminders button works
entries.preview: The overdue digest's new Reminders button now opens your reminder list with one tap.
entries.summary: A small follow-up before the overdue digest template goes live. The approved template carries a Reminders button, and we confirmed it is a Quick Reply - the kind that simply sends its own text back when tapped, with no link and no parameters. The send now includes it in exactly that form, so it can never be rejected for a missing button parameter. Tapping Reminders opens your reminder list straight away - the same answer you get by typing reminders - so the digest always has one clear next step. Nobody sees anything different until the template is switched on.

entries.title: Your earnings stay yours
entries.preview: Hand a vehicle to a buyer without losing your earnings - and overdue documents now arrive as one clear digest.
entries.summary: Two real fixes. First: when you hand a vehicle to a buyer through a passbook transfer, your earnings history for that vehicle now stays yours. Before, the moment the handover completed, your own earnings vanished from your records while the new owner could see figures they never earned. Now that history is archived at the handover, the buyer never sees it, and you can open it any time under Records - Transferred (history) on your dashboard. About ten minutes after the handover you also receive a final earnings report by email, with the same report attached as a PDF and a link back to the history view. If anything goes wrong while finalizing the handover, the transfer stops cleanly and nothing changes. Second: overdue compliance documents no longer arrive as a burst of one message per item. The first overdue item still tells you immediately; after that you get one clear digest three days later and one a week later, naming how many items are overdue, the oldest one and how long it has been past due - at most three messages per episode, no matter how many documents are late. Renew everything and the countdown stops. As always, reply reminders any time for the full list.

entries.title: A stronger superadmin console
entries.preview: Six carefully guarded admin tools: view a passbook, extend a trial, help a handover, email as Saka and more.
entries.summary: This release gives the superadmin real tools on the web console, each behind a typed confirmation, a written reason and an audit trail. You can now open a passbook to check the plate, VIN and handover history (identifiers stay masked until revealed); extend an account trial, always within the engine's own limit; reset a profile for a clean sign-up, which also ends every live session that profile owned; and facilitate a passbook handover through its first three steps, with the release PIN going only to the owner. Support messages can be sent as Saka Fleet from the console, with a preview first and a typed confirmation before anything leaves. There is also a read-only impersonation: the superadmin can look at an owner's dashboard for 30 minutes behind a yellow banner, cannot change anything while there, and exiting never signs them out. Every action lands in the audit log with who, what, why and the before/after values.

entries.title: Hardened at the edge
entries.preview: Safer spreadsheets, no internal errors on screen, HTTPS everywhere and fair rate limits for every account.
entries.summary: Behind-the-scenes hardening with four things you can feel. First: exported spreadsheets can no longer run a hidden formula - an expense note or label that starts with =, +, - or @ is exported as plain text, while real numbers stay numbers and still add up. Second: if something goes wrong on our side, the screen now shows one calm line instead of a technical message, and the full detail goes straight to the engineering log where it belongs. Third: the dashboard and API now require HTTPS end to end and tell browsers to remember it, so nobody can be silently downgraded to plain HTTP. Fourth: sign-in codes now reuse the same cross-site protection every other dashboard action already had. And behind all of it, rate limits are now counted per person instead of per shared network address, so one busy account can never lock the sign-in page for everyone else. Nothing you type changes - every flow, report and dashboard page behaves exactly as before.

entries.title: Nicknames you can actually change
entries.preview: Say "edit KAS 628T nickname to The Workhorse" and it is done in one message.
entries.summary: Last release gave every vehicle a nickname, but the edit screen never learned about it - asking to change a nickname was politely refused again and again, and the name was never saved. That is fixed. Nickname is now a real field when you edit a vehicle: say "edit KAS 628T nickname" and Saka asks only for the new name, or say the whole thing at once - "edit KAS 628T nickname to The Workhorse" or "rename KAS 628T to The Workhorse" - and it is done in one message. Changed your mind about a name? Reply remove and the vehicle goes back to showing its plate. Everything else stays exactly where it was: the nickname still leads every confirmation, log and dashboard line, and the VIN and passbook token remain locked forever.

entries.title: A release gate that stays honest
entries.preview: One check compared bytes, not words - so a Windows checkout looked like a change that never happened.
entries.summary: Housekeeping with a purpose: one of Saka's own quality checks compared text files byte-for-byte, and a Windows checkout hands the very same text back with slightly different invisible line endings. The check called that 'drift' even though nothing had changed, and it made the pre-deploy health gate fail on a clean machine. It now compares the actual words, so identical content always reads as identical, while a real change still fails the gate. Nothing you see in WhatsApp, reports or the dashboard changes.

entries.title: Saka learns your fleet's names
entries.preview: Give any vehicle a nickname — 'The Workhorse' — and every log, report and dashboard speaks it.
entries.summary: Two additions that make Saka feel like part of your garage. First: every asset can now carry a nickname - up to 40 characters, set during registration (just reply skip if you do not want one) or later when editing the vehicle. From then on the nickname is the name that shows everywhere: confirmations read 'Logged for The Workhorse (KAS 628T)', the fleet list and vehicle pages lead with it, and you can simply say 'log fuel for The Workhorse' - the engine looks for a nickname first, then the plate, then the serial, then the make and model. If two vehicles were given the same nickname Saka asks which one, and it never guesses one from a sentence. Second: voice notes now understand each country's own language from a knowledge base row - Kenya's Swahili + English pair stays the default, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, France, Germany, Spain and Belgium each lead with their own language, and every other country leads with its regional language, English first. An operator can retune any country's voice language without a new release. Both changes are live: the columns exist, 21 countries were backfilled and audited, and nothing you already have changes.

entries.title: One ledger, one place for settings
entries.preview: The old duplicate expense write is gone, and Saka's internal settings now live under one naming scheme.
entries.summary: Housekeeping with a real payoff. Since 2026 Saka has written every expense twice: once to the real ledger, and once to an old table kept for compatibility. That old write had been failing silently for months - it named a column the table never had, the database politely refused every row, and nobody read the refusal. The old write is now deleted, so an expense is written exactly once, to the ledger your reports and dashboards read. The compatibility table is kept untouched as an archive. Separately, Saka's internal settings keys were mid-migration between an old naming style and the new namespaced one; that migration is complete, the old keys are removed, and a missing setting can no longer fall back to a stale duplicate. Nothing you see changes: reports, records, PDFs and totals read the same ledger as before - there is just one write path instead of two, and no silent failures.

entries.title: Voice notes, heard properly this time
entries.preview: A live probe of your real notes found the true cause: the rate was 48000, not 16000. All three now transcribe.
entries.summary: The first voice-note fix made Google accept the request, but it declared the wrong sample rate, so notes came back as the single word 'ah' or as silence. We downloaded the three notes you sent and replayed them against the speech service with every plausible setting. The containers themselves say 48000, and at that rate all three transcribed real words - including 'will it cost 300 Kenya shillings' and 'puncture repair'. Saka now reads the rate from each note's own audio container instead of assuming one, so WhatsApp notes on any phone transcribe correctly, and an operator can still force a rate if a future client changes format. Language coverage for mixed Swahili and English is the next improvement.

entries.title: Voice notes actually reach Saka, and Free sees a warm door
entries.preview: Voice notes now transcribe, and the Free dashboard answer is a warm plan card instead of a cold refusal.
entries.summary: Three things. First: a voice note sent today was answered with 'I can't listen to voice notes yet' even though voice transcription shipped in v1.79.0. The live log showed why: the speech service now answers, but it rejected every WhatsApp voice note because the audio configuration declared the Opus format without its sample rate, and Google refuses a rate of zero. Voice notes now declare their rate explicitly (16000, adjustable), and if one still cannot be heard the fallback line is honest about it - 'I couldn't catch that voice note - please type it or send a shorter one' - instead of pretending listening was never built. Second: typing 'dashboard' on the Free plan gave a cold 'that's a paid feature' line. The engine now answers with a warm card: the live dashboard is a paid feature, the same data is available right now as a PDF (*report*), and *subscription* shows the plans (from $9.99/month) - always a next step, never a dead end. Paid and trial accounts keep the sign-in link exactly as before, and the superadmin keeps the admin door. Third: we proved in the suite that an owner's records never disappear when a vehicle is handed to a driver - the records view is scoped to the owner's vehicles, not to who typed the entry.

entries.title: A licence stays a licence, and cancel really cancels
entries.preview: Driver's licences are no longer mistaken for logbooks — and cancelling a handover now genuinely clears it.
entries.summary: Two walkthrough fixes. First: sending your driver's licence could be mistaken for a vehicle logbook. A Kenyan licence prints a long serial number, and Saka's reader treated any long number as a vehicle identification number, so the licence was filed as a vehicle document instead of a driver document. Licence wording now wins over logbook wording, a vehicle identification number must contain both letters and digits (a plain serial is not one), and the dashboard reader was hardened so a licence can never be filed as a logbook again. The licence number and expiry are read correctly for your driver record, and real logbooks still parse exactly as before — including one crash in the logbook reader that could quietly drop every hint, now fixed. Second: cancelling a pending passbook handover said 'cancelled' but left it in flight, blocking a new handover. The cancel was writing a database field that does not exist, the failure was silent, and the page still said success. Cancel now writes exactly what the database holds, a failure is reported honestly, and a paused handover (buyer needs more garage space) now also blocks a duplicate. Your stuck walkthrough handover was cleaned up so you can start a fresh one. Nothing else moved: no new tables, no data model change.

entries.title: Your stored files and receipts, where you can see them
entries.preview: Vehicle pages now list every stored logbook, insurance and inspection file — and receipts stay linked to expenses.
entries.summary: Two real bugs from a live walkthrough, both fixed at the root. First: send Saka a logbook or insurance photo and the file was safely stored — but your vehicle page never showed it, because the page asked for the list in a shape the storage service did not recognise and quietly got nothing back. The page now asks correctly, and a new safety net means that mistake can never be silent again: every vehicle page lists its current files with View and Delete. Second: send a fuel receipt photo and, once you confirmed the expense, the record could not show you the receipt picture. Two things had gone wrong: the confirmation quiz never started from the photo itself (Saka asked you to type the details instead), so the saved expense lost its link to the receipt; and a Kenyan fiscal receipt's money format was misread, so the receipt's amount was recorded as the shop's P.O. Box number instead of the total. Now a receipt photo always opens the confirmation card itself, the saved expense carries its receipt link, and Kenyan fiscal amounts read correctly (a plain GLOBAL receipt behaves exactly as before). The passbook transfer page also stopped silently listing nothing. We repaired the two walkthrough records too: the fuel expense now shows its receipt, and the insurance certificate was re-fetched and stored with its dates. One known gap, next release: a document sent before your first vehicle exists is still not kept.

entries.title: The verification code button, fixed
entries.preview: A live test caught a missing button parameter in the new sign-in code template. Fixed and re-proven.
entries.summary: A small hotfix with a good story: after switching the WhatsApp sign-in code onto an approved verification template, a real send to the test number was rejected by WhatsApp because the approved template includes a button that also needs the code. Our message carried the code in the text but not in the button, so WhatsApp refused it. The fix teaches Saka's template registry that a template can have buttons and passes the code to them as well; if a code were ever missing, the message now falls back to the plain text version instead of failing. The other two templates - the driver invitation and the passbook buyer invitation - sent correctly on the first live attempt, and the code delivery is now proven end to end against WhatsApp itself. Nothing else changed.

entries.title: When email stops, you will know
entries.preview: If the email service runs out of quota, Saka now tells you on WhatsApp and on the command center.
entries.summary: Email is how Saka sends verification codes, transfer release PINs, trial reminders and Amina's replies - and the email provider has a daily limit. When that limit is hit, the provider refuses politely and everything downstream simply stops, quietly. This release makes that failure loud. Every single email Saka sends now goes through one guard: the moment it sees the provider's quota or rate-limit response, it records the day once, writes an audit entry, and sends the operator one WhatsApp message saying the quota is exhausted and email resumes at midnight UTC. The operator's command center shows a red banner for the rest of that UTC day, and it disappears on its own when the quota resets - an old warning is never shown as today's outage. Nothing about your emails, codes or data changed; the point is that a silent outage becomes a five-second read.

entries.title: Sign in even after a day away
entries.preview: Your sign-in code now arrives even after a day away - and so do driver and buyer invitations.
entries.summary: WhatsApp only lets a business send a free message to someone who has messaged it in the last 24 hours. Outside that window the message is dropped without an error - which meant a returning user could ask for their dashboard sign-in code, see 'code sent', and never receive it. This release moves the sign-in code onto an approved WhatsApp verification template, so it arrives whenever you ask, however long you have been away. The same treatment goes to the two invitations Saka sends on someone else's behalf: a newly assigned driver is invited to accept the vehicle, and a passbook buyer is invited to accept a handover - both previously free-form, both easy for WhatsApp to drop because those people had often never messaged Saka at all. Nothing changes until the operator approves the templates in Meta; until then every message is exactly what it was before. The words Saka uses did not change either: your code, your invitations, your transfer flow.

entries.title: Your trial, told straight
entries.preview: The welcome message now shows your real trial length and its real end date — including the 6-month launch award.
entries.summary: A small release about one important thing: the words Saka uses about your trial. If you were one of the first 50 sign-ups, your welcome card could say six months while a second line quoted a date only thirty days away - both from the same message. That is fixed. The card now reads the trial as it actually stands after the launch award is applied, so a 6-month welcome trial shows its true end date, and a standard trial shows the normal 30-day window with no award message being claimed unless it was really granted. The pre-save summary also stopped repeating an old line about a per-vehicle trial: trials belong to your account, once, and never to a VIN. If Saka ever cannot read the live end date, it now says fewer words rather than a wrong date. Nothing about billing, prices or your data changed.

entries.title: The command center, and a handover that speaks the machine
entries.preview: Revenue, churn, support and AI spend in one command center - and handovers that say Operator, Captain or Rider.
entries.summary: This release is about the things you only notice when they are wrong. First, compliance: a truck or a bus in Kenya now gets its PSV badge tracked properly. Until now Saka stored every road asset under one vehicle class internally, so trucks and buses quietly missed the PSV requirement - that is fixed, and a commercial truck is recognised as a PSV under the Traffic Act. Second, reports: a generator or a boat no longer shows an 'Odometer' column. PDFs, the vehicle snapshot and the admin fleet table now use each asset's own meter - Odometer for cars, Engine hours for machines and boats, and 'Reading' when a garage has both. Third, signing in: the login page fills in your country code based on where you are, an already-signed-in visitor goes straight to their dashboard, and logging out brings you back to the sign-in page with a friendly note instead of a dead end. Fourth, documents: when you upload a renewed insurance certificate or logbook, it replaces the previous one instead of piling up - the old file is kept in a 'Show replaced' history so you can still show it to a buyer or an officer. Fifth, handovers now use the right word for the machine: a car has a Driver, a boda a Rider, a generator or excavator an Operator and a boat a Captain, and the reading asked for is engine hours where that is what the machine measures. For the operator there is a new command center: a dashboard page and an 'admin command' message that show active paid accounts, estimated monthly revenue (list prices, never an invoice), trials ending within three days, past-due and churned accounts, accounts with no assets, open and escalated support tickets, and AI spend per active account with the off-peak savings - plus the same numbers in the 8am briefing, in full on Mondays. The website also gained a Log In button in the header and a quiet King link in the footer for the operator's own door.

entries.title: Every machine speaks its own language
entries.preview: Generators, excavators and boats now show engine hours and cost per hour - not an odometer they do not have.
entries.summary: Saka has always logged whatever you run. This release makes the whole product speak each asset's own language. Your dashboard now shows the right meter everywhere: cars, motorcycles, trucks and buses show the odometer with tyre wear and cost per kilometre, while generators, machinery, heavy equipment and boats show engine hours with service intervals and cost per operating hour. Handing a machine to an operator asks for engine hours at handover, never a made-up mileage. The records view and CSV import follow the fleet too: an hours-based fleet imports and exports engine hours, and the readings stay in your notes exactly as Saka writes them in chat. Two more countries are properly supported: Belgian numbers (+32) get euros, Dutch-Belgian formatting and Belgian rules, and Canadian owners can set Canada once (country Canada) to get Canadian dollars, Canadian dates and provincial rules - it needs that one explicit choice because Canada shares the +1 prefix with the US. Drivers in the UK, US, Canada, the UAE, India and Australia now see their real professional documents (Driver CPC, CDL, heavy vehicle permits, HR licences and white cards) instead of a generic card. Passbook handovers quote their fee in the buyer's own currency, and machines hand over by serial number. Everything you already logged stays exactly as it was.

entries.title: Your logbook, insurance and inspection files stay on file
entries.preview: Send a logbook, insurance or inspection photo - Saka keeps the original. View or download it from your dashboard.
entries.summary: Until now Saka read your documents, saved the dates and then let the photo go. That changes now. Send a photo or PDF of your logbook, insurance certificate, inspection certificate or road licence and Saka reads it exactly as before - and keeps the original file for you. Open the vehicle page on your dashboard and you will find a new Stored files section: every certificate with the date you sent it, a View button that opens a private, short-lived link, and a Delete button if you ever want the file gone (your dates and reminders stay exactly where they are). The compliance page now shows how many files are on record for each vehicle. In WhatsApp, reply documents to see your stored files numbered, and delete document 2 DELETE to remove one - same careful confirm step as receipts. Paid plans and the welcome trial keep the original file; the free plan keeps the figures it read but not the file itself, and the page tells you so honestly. Each stored file is also linked to the insurance, inspection or licence it proves, so you always know where a date came from.

entries.title: Sharper dashboard, transfers and your plan in one place
entries.preview: The dashboard now wears the Saka look, and you can hand over a passbook and manage your plan without leaving it.
entries.summary: Your dashboard has grown up. It now wears the same Saka brand as the website - the real logo, the premium type and a calm green glow - and it feels right on a phone, with bigger buttons and readable forms. Two new pages do real work. Passbook transfer lets you hand a vehicle to a buyer from the dashboard: pick the car, enter the buyer's WhatsApp number, email and the handover mileage, then type the 6-digit release PIN Saka emails you. The buyer still accepts on WhatsApp and enters their own emailed code, so nothing moves without both of you. If your account has no email yet, the page tells you honestly and points you to the one-line fix. Subscription shows your plan, status, trial end, vehicle slots and billing history, and lets you upgrade or add extra Fleet Command slots through the same secure Paystack checkout - Saka never invents a price or a payment outcome. The Add Vehicle button opens WhatsApp with 'add car' ready to send, because registration still happens in chat where Saka can guide you step by step. Your PDF reports also pick up the new look, with the same clear margins whether you read them on a laptop or a phone.

entries.title: Sign in to your dashboard right from WhatsApp
entries.preview: Open your dashboard with a code sent straight to WhatsApp - no email needed.
entries.summary: Signing in to your dashboard is now quicker and fits how you already use Saka. Message "dashboard" (or "records") and Saka sends you a sign-in link; open it, type your WhatsApp number, and a 6-digit code arrives in your WhatsApp chat. Type the code on the page and you are in for 15 minutes - no email, no waiting, no password to remember. If you are not signed up yet, the page tells you honestly and points you to the quick sign-up. The same link works for drivers (when they are assigned to a vehicle), and there is a separate, private entrance for the Saka team. Behind the scenes, the team's internal profiles report now counts real accounts instead of empty first-contact rows, so the numbers the team sees come from real fleets only. Everything else - your records, reports, reminders and documents - is unchanged.

entries.title: Bring your history in, and receipts that stay attached
entries.preview: Import old expenses from a CSV file on your dashboard - and every receipt photo now stays linked to its expense.
entries.summary: Two practical additions. First, your dashboard has a new Import page: upload (or paste) a CSV with Date, Vehicle Plate, Type, Amount, Odometer and Notes, and Saka checks every row - the plate must be one of your vehicles, the type must be a real expense type, the amount must be positive, the date must be readable and not in the future, and rows that repeat each other or something you logged in the last few hours are flagged - then shows you a preview with problem rows highlighted. Nothing is saved until you confirm, and only the clean rows are saved. Importing historical expenses never starts or extends a trial and never uses your report allowance. Second, a receipt photo you send now stays permanently attached to the expense it created: the Records page shows the receipt for exactly the right row instead of guessing from the vehicle, date and amount. Older receipts still find their expense the old way, and the team can backfill them safely.

entries.title: Support that investigates before it replies
entries.preview: Support emails are investigated by Amina before she answers - plus tyre wear and cost-per-km on your dashboard.
entries.summary: Two improvements this release. First, support email gets a real investigator: Amina reads your message, checks your account, your vehicles, any recent errors and what you were last doing in WhatsApp, then either answers you directly or hands your case to a human with everything she found already written down. She never discusses money, refunds or account changes on her own - those go straight to a person, as before. Second, the dashboard has a new Analytics page: it shows how much life is left on your tyres (based on the odometer you logged at your last tyre change) and how your cost per kilometre has moved over the last six months. Both pages are read-only, calculated by the same engine as your reports, and your records are unchanged.

entries.title: Talk to Saka: voice notes now work
entries.preview: Send a voice note and Saka understands it - log fuel, ask a question or answer a quiz by speaking.
entries.summary: You can now send a voice note instead of typing. Saka listens, turns your words into a normal message, and handles it exactly as if you had typed it: log a fuel stop while you are at the pump, ask about your week, or answer a quiz question out loud. Notes up to about a minute work best, and Kenyan numbers understand both Swahili and English (English elsewhere). If a note cannot be heard - too long, or the line was unclear - Saka says so honestly and asks you to type it instead, and nothing is ever saved from a note it could not understand. Your records, reports and reminders are unchanged: this release simply adds an easier way to talk to Saka.

entries.title: Clearer release notices
entries.preview: Behind the scenes: every release announcement now names the exact version and revision.
entries.summary: A small behind-the-scenes improvement. When a new version of Saka goes live, the internal notification now carries the exact version number and the Cloud Run revision id, so the team can confirm at a glance which build is serving your conversations. Nothing changed in how you use Saka: your records, reports and reminders behave exactly as before.

entries.title: Your numbers, in your country's format
entries.preview: Older accounts now show the right currency, dates and timezone - plus faster behind-the-scenes checks.
entries.summary: Two quiet improvements this week. First: every account now shows money, dates and times in its own country's format, including the accounts created before those settings existed - if you signed up early, your reports and answers now use your local currency and timezone instead of a generic default. Second, the Saka team can now check system health, AI usage and the fix backlog by simply asking in plain English, so issues get noticed and handled faster. Nothing about your records changed: this release is about the right numbers in the right place, and a team that can see problems sooner.

entries.title: Your month, in your inbox
entries.preview: Switch on a monthly PDF summary - and every report in chat now opens instantly on your dashboard.
entries.summary: Two things changed, both about getting your numbers faster. First: a Monthly PDF summary you can switch on (in the dashboard Settings page, or by replying monthly report on in WhatsApp). On the 1st of every month at 8:00 AM you get one email with your fleet's month as a branded PDF attached - spend, earnings, net, fuel, distance and where the money went, covering the month that just ended. It never uses your monthly report quota, and it is completely separate from the Monday text summary, so you can have either, both or neither. Second: asking for a report in chat is now instant. Instead of waiting while the report is built in the background, Saka answers immediately with the link to your dashboard Reports page, where every PDF downloads on the spot - and when the file builds quickly enough, the PDF link comes in that same reply. Nothing is emailed on demand any more, so your inbox only ever carries the monthly summary you asked for (plus the vehicle summary PDF when you explicitly request it). Your weekly Monday summary is unchanged. The dashboard remains switched off in production until the walk-through is signed off.

entries.title: A dashboard for everyone on the fleet
entries.preview: Drivers get their own page, and the right people can see every fleet at a glance - safely.
entries.summary: The dashboard now has three doors. Owners keep the full toolkit they just received. Drivers, once you assign them to a vehicle, can reply dashboard in WhatsApp and get a private link to their own page: the vehicle they drive, their own licence, PSV badge and medical documents with the real numbers, and their last week of fuel, spend and earnings - and nothing belonging to anyone else. If a driver is no longer assigned, their link simply stops working; the message tells them to ask you for an assignment. The superadmin (and only the superadmin) can reply dashboard admin to see every owner with a fleet, with phone numbers masked, and open any one fleet read-only - and every single visit is recorded in the audit log, so cross-fleet access is never invisible. Owner pages, driver pages and admin pages are strictly separated: a driver who tries an owner page is politely turned away, and anyone who is not the superadmin simply sees that the admin page does not exist. The dashboard stays switched off in production until the walk-through is signed off. Nothing about your records has changed - this is the same engine, with the right view for each person.

entries.title: Your own reports, your own copy of everything
entries.preview: Build the exact report you want, switch the Monday summary on or off, and download every record in one file.
entries.summary: The dashboard is finished. There is now a Reports page where you pick the period - this month, the last 30 days, this year or your own dates - tick the vehicles you care about and choose up to eight numbers, then the PDF downloads straight away, built by the same engine behind your WhatsApp reports. There is also a Settings page: switch the Monday morning summary on or off with one tap (the same switch WhatsApp uses, so they always agree), and download every record you have - expenses, earnings, reminders, vehicle documents, driver documents and receipt records - in a single file that opens cleanly in Excel, with each section clearly labelled. Your plan sits there too, with a pointer to reply subscription in chat when you want to change it. Reports built here never use your monthly report quota, and only your own fleet is ever included. The dashboard stays switched off in production until the walk-through is signed off - when it opens, this is the complete owner toolkit: overview, vehicles, records, compliance, reports and settings.

entries.title: Every document, one calm view
entries.preview: See what is expired, what is due in the next 30 days and who still needs to renew - for every vehicle and every driver.
entries.summary: Your dashboard now has a Compliance page. It lists each vehicle and each assigned driver with what Saka is tracking, the next document to fall due, and a simple colour: red for expired, orange for due, green for valid, grey for missing. Three filters do the thinking for you - All, Due soon (30 days) and Expired - and anything already lapsed stays at the top of the list. Tap a driver and you get their own page: name, phone, their vehicle, and every document they have on file with its number and expiry, in full, so you can verify a licence or a badge without hunting through chats. The PDF button exports exactly the view you are looking at, so a compliance check can be printed or shared in one step. Everything comes from the documents you already saved in WhatsApp; nothing is estimated, and only your own fleet is ever shown. The dashboard remains switched off in production until the walk-through is signed off.

entries.title: Every record, searchable and exportable
entries.preview: Search and filter your whole ledger by date, type, vehicle or label - then download exactly what you see as CSV or PDF.
entries.summary: Your dashboard now has a Records page: every fuel stop, repair and earning across your fleet, newest first, twenty at a time. Narrow it by date range, expense type, vehicle, label or a keyword from the notes; the page keeps your filters in the link so you can share or revisit the same view, and the arrows move you through older entries. When a photo receipt belongs to a row - one clear match and no ambiguity - a View link opens the image through a private five-minute link. The CSV download opens neatly in Excel, and the PDF is the same professional ledger you already know, built from exactly the filter you chose. Only your own fleet is ever included. The dashboard remains switched off in production while we finish the walk-through.

entries.title: Your vehicles, each with its own page
entries.preview: Open your dashboard and see every vehicle, what is coming due, and what each one has cost you this month.
entries.summary: The dashboard now opens onto your fleet. One list shows every vehicle with its plate and model, whether it is active or paused, its odometer, its driver, what it has cost you this month and the very next document coming due. Tap any vehicle and you get its own page: the odometer, this month's spend and earnings, every document Saka tracks for it with how long is left, and its eight most recent records - fuel, repairs, earnings - each with its amount and date. Everything is in your own currency and units, and only ever your own fleet. The dashboard is still switched off in production while we finish the walk-through; your PDF reports stay one message away in WhatsApp.

entries.title: Your dashboard, built
entries.preview: The page is ready: your spending, earnings, what is coming up and your latest activity, in one private place.
entries.summary: The dashboard's one page is finished. Open the link Saka emails you, enter the 6-digit code from that same email, and you land on a private overview: what you have spent and earned, your net, how many vehicles are active, the six documents coming due soonest and your five most recent entries. It is a quiet, readable page made for a phone screen. The dashboard is switched off in production for one final walk-through and will open to everyone in the next phase; your PDF reports stay exactly where they are, one message away in WhatsApp.

entries.title: One word opens your dashboard
entries.preview: Reply *dashboard* and Saka emails you a private link plus a 6-digit code - the code never appears in WhatsApp.
entries.summary: The dashboard's front door is live behind the scenes. Reply *dashboard* in WhatsApp and Saka emails you a private link that works for 15 minutes, together with a 6-digit code. The link opens a page where you enter that code; it only ever arrives by email, and Saka will never ask you for it in the chat. If you are still on the Free plan the request politely points you to the plans instead. The page itself is being finished in the next release - if you ask today, Saka will simply say the dashboard is not ready yet.

entries.title: Groundwork for your dashboard
entries.preview: We are building a web dashboard where your fleet's numbers will live. This release lays the secure foundation behind it.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes release. Saka's reports are growing a permanent home on the web: a private dashboard page you will open from a link Saka emails you, protected by a 6-digit code that only ever arrives in your inbox - never in WhatsApp. This release builds the secure sign-in plumbing (short-lived links, hashed codes, private sessions) and the shared page styling the full dashboard will use. Nothing changes in your WhatsApp chats yet, and the dashboard stays switched off until the next phases are ready.

entries.title: Template buttons, handled
entries.preview: Tap a quick-reply button on a reminder or plan message and Saka treats it as your typed reply.
entries.summary: A defensive, behind-the-scenes release. Some of Saka's proactive templates may in future arrive with quick-reply buttons (like "Reminders" or "Subscription"). If you tap one, Saka now treats it as the typed reply you would otherwise send - the same reminders list, plan summary or help menu opens, and quick-edit buttons keep their existing safety locks. A button we do not recognise falls back to its own title, and any shape Saka cannot read is recorded for the team to diagnose instead of being guessed at. Nothing changes for normal typed chats, photos or voice notes.

entries.title: Quieter quality reports, nothing missed
entries.preview: Saka's quality checks now land in one six-hourly summary instead of interrupting - and a delayed summary says so.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes reliability release for the team that tunes Saka's conversation quality. Judge hiccups (a moment where an answer could not be scored) no longer trigger instant alerts; each one is recorded with its case and reason and lands in the six-hourly quality summary, which also lists every heal, proposal and failed heal - so nothing is lost and nothing interrupts. If the summary email cannot go out, the team now gets one short WhatsApp note saying it will retry in 15 minutes. Nothing you see in chat changes.

entries.title: Every driver document, one reminder each
entries.preview: PSV badges, PDPs, CPCs, operator cards and medicals now get their own expiry reminders - and duplicate alerts are gone.
entries.summary: Your driver documents are now fully covered: every licence, PSV badge, PDP, CPC, operator card and medical certificate with an expiry date gets its own reminder with the familiar 30-day, 14-day, 7-day, 24-hour and overdue steps. Each document keeps its own countdown, so a PSV badge and a PDP can never hide each other. The release also fixes a noisy bug found in a deep audit: the background sync re-saved reminders every 30 minutes with their notification marks wiped, so the same alert could fire repeatedly. Now only a real expiry-date change resets the countdown - a renewed document alerts once per step, a lifetime document needs no reminder, and nothing expired is ever revived into a new alert. Nothing you see changes, except fewer duplicate reminders.

entries.title: A cleaner engine room, same Saka
entries.preview: Internal cleanup: the older sign-up lane moved to its own module; the trial downsizing check now passes every run.
entries.summary: A pure housekeeping release. Saka's older two-step vehicle sign-up lane (kept as a fallback behind the modern registration quiz) moved into its own module - every reply, step and message is byte-for-byte identical, proven line by line. The internal quality gate also gained the authoritative facts it was missing when judging the trial-end downsizing card (which asset stays, which plan fits, the pause-never-delete promise), so that check now passes cleanly every run instead of flip-flopping. Nothing you see changes - and the full suite plus the live health audit are green.

entries.title: More pages, your tickets, weekly reports
entries.preview: Reply "more" to page older entries and receipts, check your own support tickets, and opt into a Monday fleet summary.
entries.summary: Three everyday conveniences: "more" now pages older entries (6 at a time) and receipts (5 at a time) - paged rows are view-only, so editing and deleting always point at your newest list. "my ticket" shows the last three tickets you opened with our team, with status and last update. And "weekly report on" sends you a one-message fleet summary every Monday at 8am - text only, never using your report quota; "weekly report off" stops it.

entries.title: Your trial, answered straight
entries.preview: Ask "trial status" or "my trial" and Saka answers with your own days left - instantly, with no detour.
entries.summary: A small routing fix with a big clarity win: short trial questions ("trial", "trial status", "my trial") now go straight to your own plan summary - the days left, your asset slots and your report quota - instead of a general marketing note. Longer sentences like "my trial ended, what now?" keep their own guided flow, and nothing else changes. Behind the scenes the quality suite also gained a new calibration test that proves the evaluation gate can catch an invented earnings amount.

entries.title: Steadier housekeeping, same Saka
entries.preview: Saka's internal settings now live under clear names - every reminder, digest and alert keeps working as before.
entries.summary: A behind-the-scenes tidy-up: Saka's internal settings (its learned tone notes, deploy markers, digest and alert timers) now live under clear, grouped names. During the transition every setting is read from both the old and the new name and written to both, so a deploy can never miss a reminder or repeat an alert. The migration copies every existing setting into its new name and keeps the old one until the next release - nothing you see changes, proven by the full quality suite.

entries.title: Counted once, counted right
entries.preview: Fleet totals in admin reports now match reality - every expense is counted exactly once.
entries.summary: The executive report briefly counted each expense twice: Saka writes your ledger and kept an older mirror copy, and the report added both together. The report now reads the one real ledger, so expense totals, net profit and per-vehicle passbooks all match reality. A behind-the-scenes flag also prepares the retirement of that old mirror copy - nothing you see changes, and every record, report and reply works exactly as before, proven by the full quality suite.

entries.title: A quiet tidy-up behind the scenes
entries.preview: One unused leftover from an older edit flow was removed - every answer, record and report stays exactly the same.
entries.summary: A small internal cleanup: the old in-place entry editor was retired when corrections became delete-and-re-log, and the leftover code has now been removed. Saka's ledger, records, reports and replies are completely unchanged - proven by the full quality suite.

entries.title: A whole week to choose your plan
entries.preview: The plan that fits your assets now arrives 3 days before your trial ends - and you are never shown the same price twice.
entries.summary: Three days before your trial ends, Saka now sends the plan that fits your garage - the tier for your asset count, your local price and a working payment link - so you have a full week to decide instead of a few days. When the trial ends, the reminder is a gentle nudge: it repeats the price and link only if your fleet changed and the plan is different; otherwise it simply keeps the choice open and points back to the link you already have. Accounts with a failed or cancelled payment are quietly spared the sales nudges, and a payment link also triggers up to three gentle reminders to help you finish. Proven by the full quality suite.

entries.title: Saka's quick thinking gets the fast lane
entries.preview: Every quick check now uses the lighter model, so Saka costs less to run while big answers stay premium.
entries.summary: Saka now uses the lighter model for every quick, repeatable check - including the first read of what you are asking - while the answers that matter (your data, pricing, complaints, parsing your logs) keep the strongest model. The quality checks that guard Saka were also made steadier: they now average several runs so one noisy score can no longer freeze a good improvement. Proven by the full quality suite and a three-run conversation eval gate.

entries.title: Saka's quick notes get the fast pen
entries.preview: Quick, repeatable messages now use the lighter model - the important answers keep the best one.
entries.summary: Saka now picks the right-sized brain for each job. The quick, repeatable bits - quiz prompts, little nudges, one-line small talk - run on the lighter model on every plan, while the answers that matter (your own data, pricing, complaints, parsing your logs) keep the best one. A quiet cleanup also fixed a hidden wiring issue so the complaint lane keeps its full-quality model no matter what. Proven by the full quality suite and the conversation eval gate.

entries.title: The last four rooms get their own doors
entries.preview: Commands, admin, the AI turn and support intake now live in tidy files - same answers, same order, unchanged.
entries.summary: The final four backstage jobs moved into their own clear files. The first runs every straight command - country, receipts, passbook, reports, quick logs, vehicle and profile edits. The second holds the team gates: the care console and the admin console. The third runs the real conversation: the AI turn plus the honest answers to questions, complaints, feedback and greetings. The fourth catches every support request. A written rule keeps them leaves - they hand data back and never reach into the main file - and the loop-breaker, the slow-turn ack, onboarding and the final polish stay in the orchestrator where they belong. Nothing you see changes: proven by comparing 1,106 moved code lines against the previous release (99.9 percent identical, one wiring-only difference) and the full quality suite.

entries.title: Three steady hands keep the conversation on track
entries.preview: Read answers, waiting steps and quiz turns now live in tidy files - same answers, same order, unchanged.
entries.summary: Three more of Saka's busiest jobs moved into their own clear files. The first answers every straight question - reminders, compliance, your ledger, receipts and mileage - through one ordered map. The second holds every 'waiting on you' step: a CLEAR confirmation, a support note, a passbook handover, a security code, a document capture, a multi-record save, a deletion yes/no. The third runs the quiz: how a draft pauses for a chat, how it parks when you change your mind, and how a finished flow is confirmed. A written rule keeps the order exactly as it was - reads first, waiting steps in their old positions around the quiz - and the background loop-breaker stays in the main file where it belongs. Nothing you see changes: proven by comparing 899 moved code lines against the previous release (88 percent identical, the rest are wiring-only) and the full quality suite.

entries.title: A tidier intake desk and a steadier rhythm
entries.preview: Saka's photo intake and per-turn habits now live in their own tidy files - same answers, same speed, unchanged.
entries.summary: Two more of Saka's busy backstage jobs moved into their own clear files. The first is the documents desk: reading every photo and PDF you send, checking for duplicates, storing receipts and pre-filling registration forms. The second is the steady per-turn rhythm: keeping the conversation's memory, saving the transcript, queuing slow reports and timing each reply. A written rule now keeps these files leaf modules - they hand data back and never reach into the main conversation file - while every send, menu and question stays exactly where it was. Nothing you see changes: proven by comparing 179 moved code lines against the previous release (97 percent identical, the four differences are wiring-only) and the full quality suite.

entries.title: A neater workshop for Saka's tools
entries.preview: Saka's behind-the-scenes tools now live in their own tidy drawers - same answers, same speed, same behaviour.
entries.summary: The little helpers that power Saka - detecting your country and language, reading amounts and odometer figures from your words, and building your role-aware menu - together with the sender that delivers every WhatsApp reply, now live in their own clear files instead of one very large one. Nothing you see changes: every reply, card and confirmation flows exactly as before, proven by a byte-for-byte comparison of the moved code and the full quality suite.

entries.title: The same Saka, in tidier rooms
entries.preview: We split Saka's WhatsApp code into tidy rooms - same answers, same speed, same behaviour.
entries.summary: Saka's WhatsApp brain lived in one very large file. It now lives in two clear rooms - one that greets Meta's messages and one that does the thinking - with a thin doorway that keeps every old entrance working. Nothing you see changes: every reply, confirmation and record flows exactly as before, proven by a byte-for-byte comparison of the moved code and the full quality suite.

entries.title: One tidy memory for every unfinished step
entries.preview: Edits, confirmations and security codes now live in one place - same behaviour, far fewer mix-ups.
entries.summary: When Saka is waiting on you - a correction to an entry, a YES to delete a vehicle, a document number, a 6-digit code - that unfinished step used to be remembered in a dozen separate pockets, each with its own timeout and its own rule. They now live in one tidy note with one rulebook. Everything behaves exactly as before: the same priorities, the same fresh-log protection, the same codes and confirms, and the same clearing rules. A 434-check harness, including a 300-turn replay against the old routing, proves nothing you see has changed.

entries.title: A sturdier map for Saka's answers
entries.preview: One ordered map decides whether a message is a read, a log or a question - same answers, fewer surprises.
entries.summary: Saka recognises dozens of everyday reads: reminders, compliance cards, expiry questions, your ledger, receipts, mileage, records and product questions. Those rules now live in one ordered list instead of a long chain of checks, so a new rule can never accidentally grab a message meant for another. Nothing you see changes: every answer routes exactly as before, now proven by 121 automated checks against a frozen copy of the old routing.

entries.title: A warmer answer when you question a figure
entries.preview: When you say a record looks wrong, Saka now checks it with you instead of just repeating it.
entries.summary: If you challenge a figure - "that cannot be right" - Saka replays the exact same record from your ledger. The replay used to open defensively ("Same record... nothing changed"); it now opens by checking it with you before showing the numbers, and still points you at my entries to fix anything that looks off. Nothing else changed: same figures, same scope, same correction path. The quality harness also learned to measure real pass rates separately from the calibration cases that are meant to fail.

entries.title: Saka always answers from your latest numbers
entries.preview: Every correction, reminder and payment now refreshes what Saka knows instantly - no more stale facts.
entries.summary: Saka keeps a short-lived memory of your facts - plan, assets, expiries, spending, reminders - so replies stay fast. Some updates used to wait up to 15 minutes before that memory refreshed; now every write (a corrected entry, a new reminder, a payment, a plan change, an onboarding detail) refreshes it immediately, and the safety window shrank to 5 minutes. Two quieter reminders - driver activity summaries and the daily fleet audit - can also now reach you outside WhatsApp's 24-hour window when their templates are approved.

entries.title: Reminders now reach you outside WhatsApp 24-hour window
entries.preview: Proactive messages ride approved WhatsApp templates, so reminders and trial nudges no longer go silent.
entries.summary: WhatsApp only allows free-form business messages inside 24 hours of your last reply; after that, reminders were silently dropped. Saka now sends every business-initiated message through an approved WhatsApp template when one is configured - service reminders, expiry alerts, trial-ending nudges, payment reminders, win-back offers, driver releases and admin alerts. With no template configured, every message is exactly what it was before: no copy changes, no surprises.

entries.title: Saka's background work now runs at half price
entries.preview: Heavy background AI jobs wait for DeepSeek's off-peak window — lower running costs, same instant replies.
entries.summary: Saka's heavy background jobs — like generating practice conversations and running quality checks — now wait for DeepSeek's off-peak window, when the same work costs half as much. Your chats, reminders and reports are untouched: live replies never wait. The admin cost digest now shows the real off-peak saving, which keeps the service lean as the fleet grows.

entries.title: Lawn mowers and machines can finally save
entries.preview: A database rule was blocking every machinery, generator and boat save — fixed, with a safe fallback.
entries.summary: Machinery, generators, boats and even hybrid cars were being rejected by an old database rule that only accepted three values, so a lawn-mower registration could never finish. That rule now accepts every asset type, and if a database ever lags behind the app again, the save falls back to a safe value instead of failing. Complaints typed on the confirmation card are treated as messages (never as the machine name), and repeated save failures now offer a human or a clean restart instead of looping.

entries.title: Grow free on trial, pick your plan at the end
entries.preview: Add as many assets as you like during the trial — when it ends, Saka offers the plan that fits them.
entries.summary: The welcome trial no longer limits how many vehicles, machines or equipment you add. When it ends nothing is paused: Saka opens a short choice window, works out the plan that fits the assets you have, and sends the exact price and a secure payment link. You can keep everything in one tap, or reply keep <plate> to shrink to a smaller plan — extra assets pause, never disappear. Coupon codes now apply the real discount they promise, and help is one short reply away on every step.

entries.title: Trial limits are honest, and voice notes get a real answer
entries.preview: A welcome trial covers 5 vehicles: the next one is refused with the exact limit and the upgrade path, never a fake save.
entries.summary: Adding a sixth vehicle during the welcome trial now says exactly what the trial covers and offers the upgrade, instead of failing late or quietly. When the trial ends your newest vehicle stays active and the rest are paused — nothing is deleted, and one short reply brings back whichever you choose. Voice notes now get a clear reply asking you to type it, and a photo Saka cannot read asks for a clearer shot or the details typed, without ever claiming a save.

entries.title: Saka remembers your fleet, not just the chat
entries.preview: At the start of every conversation Saka refreshes a snapshot of your plan, assets, expiries and spending.
entries.summary: Saka used to depend on the chat transcript for context. Now, whenever a conversation starts, the engine assembles a fresh snapshot of your own data (plan and trial, assets with expiry dates, this month's spend, driver documents and the one next step for any missing detail) and keeps it warm for 15 minutes. Every reply is grounded in those facts, and any change you make (a new asset, a logged expense, an updated document) refreshes the snapshot immediately. The snapshot holds facts only, never codes or secrets.

entries.title: Digest retries when email is temporarily unavailable
entries.preview: If the summary email cannot be sent, it retries in 15 minutes instead of waiting six hours.
entries.summary: A failed summary email (for example when the mail provider's daily limit is reached) used to mark the six-hour window as delivered, so the next summary was six hours away. A failure now records only the attempt and retries every 15 minutes until the email actually goes out; the single WhatsApp note is sent only when the email really left.

entries.title: One quiet digest, and every error now leaves a trace
entries.preview: Quality news arrives as a single 6-hour email (with one WhatsApp ping); failed saves are always logged.
entries.summary: The quality loop no longer messages you for every fix: once every six hours it emails one detailed summary of what it graded, healed and could not fix, and sends a single WhatsApp note that the email went out. Separately, every failed save or booking on the platform now writes an incident to the error log, including a machinery-registration bug found today where a bare "Retry" was being saved as the vehicle's make and model.

entries.title: Second-look grading actually runs now
entries.preview: A default-value bug had switched off the second-look check for borderline quality verdicts; it is now on and tested.
entries.summary: The second-look grading for conversations that land right at the pass mark shipped switched off: a default value was read as zero, so the extra check never fired while borderline answers kept flipping between pass and fail. The defaults are fixed and proven by a test that forces the sequence fail-then-pass, so a borderline answer really does get its second look and the better verdict wins.

entries.title: Steadier grading, and fixes that stick
entries.preview: Borderline quality verdicts get one second look, and healed answers are folded back into the test set.
entries.summary: A conversation that lands right at the pass mark is now judged a second time, so provider wobble cannot flip a good answer; the better verdict wins and the extra calls are capped per run. Successful fixes can also be written back into the offline test set with one command, so the next check verifies the fixed answer instead of re-failing the old one, while the deliberately-bad calibration cases are never touched.

entries.title: Smarter quality fixes, no repeated tickets
entries.preview: Known-bad test cases are no longer "fixed" repeatedly, and quality hints stay capped and tidy.
entries.summary: The quality loop used to keep trying to fix the same deliberately-bad test cases, minting a new hint each time. Now those calibration cases are skipped by design, a recurring case updates its existing hint instead of creating a new one, the active hint list is capped at 30 (oldest retired first, never deleted and always reversible), and the old background rule generator is switched off by default so every prompt hint is one that has been proven to improve the score.

entries.title: One tidy alert instead of an inbox full
entries.preview: Failed quality fixes are grouped into a single summary email per check, not one email each.
entries.summary: The quality loop now collects every failed fix from a single run into one summary (WhatsApp plus one email) that lists the cases, the stage they stopped at and the scores, with a pointer to the review commands. Successful fixes remain WhatsApp-only, and a clean run sends nothing at all, so the admin inbox stays quiet and the email quota is protected.

entries.title: Quieter good-news alerts, louder problems
