entries.preview: Quality fixes are announced on WhatsApp only; anything that fails or needs a human now also reaches email.
entries.summary: The quality loop used to send both WhatsApp and email for every fix it shipped. Now a successful fix or a drafted proposal is announced on WhatsApp only, keeping the inbox quiet, while a fix that could not be shipped (or a provider problem that stopped grading) reaches both WhatsApp and email with the case, the stage, the reason and the exact commands to review it. Remediation, support and security emails are unchanged.

entries.title: The brand logo is now crisp at every size
entries.preview: The supplied SAKAFLEET artwork now powers the nav, footer, tab icon, phone icon and share card.
entries.summary: The exact supplied artwork is now the single source of the logo, rebuilt into every surface the site uses: the navigation lockup (at its true 9.9:1 ratio, so it no longer looks slightly squeezed), the footer wordmark, the browser tab icon, the phone home-screen icon and the social share card on a black canvas with one lime accent. Everything is generated from one master file, so the brand stays consistent and can be refreshed in one step.

entries.title: Fuel reads answer instantly; disputed figures get the record
entries.preview: Short asks like "Fuel all time" now read your ledger, and disputing a figure replays that exact record.
entries.summary: Two records-lane fixes from live chats: a short type ask such as "Fuel all time", "Fuel list" or "fuel report" now answers straight from your logged entries (it used to be mistaken for a new expense being logged, so you had to cancel), and a challenge like "that record cannot be right" re-shows the very record you were disputing — same vehicle, same window, same numbers — instead of a fresh fleet-wide total. Phrases like "my 2 vehicles" can no longer be mistaken for a plate number.

entries.title: Quality checks now start the moment Saka boots
entries.preview: The conversation grader runs one check right after every deploy, then every 15 minutes — visible in the logs.
entries.summary: Saka's quality loop now starts 60 seconds after every boot and logs both its configuration and each run's result, so the team can see at a glance that grading is delivering. The 15-minute cadence, unlimited case budget and prompt-level healing (code fixes still need approval) are unchanged.

entries.title: Saka's quality checks run every 15 minutes
entries.preview: Live conversations are now scored continuously, and driver-document lookups, searches and photos all answer properly.
entries.summary: The quality loop now grades real conversations every 15 minutes, with no case limits, so friction is caught the same day instead of waiting for a report. Today's stuck session showed exactly where to look: 'driver compliances' in the plural, 'list all documents with expiry date' and 'search TSV2026' now answer from the document ledgers, photos of driver documents get a warm yes with confirm-before-save, and pasted licences are read properly. A new coverage audit tracks every flow and edge scenario, with 9 fresh regional edge cases added.

entries.title: Driver documents answer from their own ledger
entries.preview: Ask for your PSV badge or licence and Saka now confirms the saved record — never an empty expense search.
entries.summary: Driver documents (PSV badge, driving licence, PDP, CPC, operator card, medical) now have their own read lane: listing them shows the saved numbers and expiry dates with colour chips, and a confirmation reads "On file ✓" straight from the driver record. The vehicle compliance card also shows your driver documents, while vehicle permits (insurance, inspection, PSL) stay separate. This closes the live 5 Nov case where a submitted PSV badge existed but "list psv badge" answered from the expense ledger.

entries.title: Kenyan rehearsal batch + a cleaner judge
entries.preview: Eight Kenyan scenarios (two with M-PESA) now run on every eval — and the launch-offer audit found nothing to fix.
entries.summary: Saka now rehearses a curated set of Kenyan conversations — Sheng shorthand, M-PESA references and mid-quiz interruptions — with every case passing the quality judge at 0.90 or better. The judge learned two fair exceptions (honest 'building your report now' commitments and instant one-line logs such as 'Logged ✓'), synthetic cases are stricter only where it matters (loop avoidance), and the launch-offer audit confirmed no account was ever granted the old 365-day award, so nothing needed reconciling.

entries.title: Saka rehearses the world — 6-month launch offer
entries.preview: New scenarios in nine transport markets test Saka's ear for local shorthand, currencies and interruptions.
entries.summary: Saka now rehearses messy conversations from Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Ghana, Brazil, Mexico, the Philippines, India, the Gulf and neutral international English — local shorthand, currencies and transport words included — with every generated scenario tagged to its country and scored by the same quality judge. The launch offer also changes: the first 50 signups now get a full 6-month trial instead of 365 days, still card-free.

entries.title: Saka grades its own conversations
entries.preview: Every reply is now scored for clarity, tone and honesty — and the small fixes are tested before anyone sees them.
entries.summary: Saka's conversations are now graded automatically on five things that matter: no repeating the same question, a warm human voice, exact shorthand handling, one question at a time, and never inventing a VIN, price, date or code. Real stuck-chat transcripts join a fixed set of tricky scenarios (hurried shorthand, interruptions, complaints, plain-language asks) for every check. When a reply fails, Saka writes one small behavioural fix, proves the corrected reply scores better, and applies it immediately — code changes still need a human approval first. Superadmins get a WhatsApp and email note for every fix, and the whole loop is off by default until switched on.

entries.title: Saka loosens up
entries.preview: Fewer robotic checks, sharper expense types, labels on everything — and a calmer, native-scroll site.
entries.summary: Review cards open with a rotating human line instead of the same template, quiz menus are shorter, and empty answers encourage instead of reporting zeros. Twenty-five expense types now cover licences, security, loading, weighbridge, hire and route fees properly. Every receipt, reminder and odometer reading can carry your own label — search any keyword to find them. Support emails also keep their real message body now, and the site scrolls natively with no install prompt.

entries.title: The new SAKAFLEET lockup
entries.preview: The real logo in the header, and softer white everywhere — same site, easier on the eyes.
entries.summary: The supplied SAKAFLEET logo (interlocking mark plus heavy uppercase wordmark) is now the site logo, and every icon and the share cover were rebuilt from it. White was dialled down across the board — text, buttons, glows and the logo itself — so nothing glares on the black canvas. The nav lockup now renders at its true wide ratio and shrinks cleanly on phones.

entries.title: Monochrome, like the logo
entries.preview: New look: the logo's black-and-white world, one lime spark, and premium Sora + Manrope type.
entries.summary: The website now wears the Sakafleet logo's own palette: a near-black canvas, white type, hairline borders and a single lime accent for links, focus rings and the popular plan. Headlines and body are set in Sora and Manrope (self-hosted, no third-party calls), the logo lockup is rebuilt from the real artwork, and a ghosted pair of the logo's fluid marks sits behind the hero. Nothing about how the site works changed.

entries.title: Saka picks up where you left off
entries.preview: Returning after a break? Saka now remembers your last few messages — and PDF links arrive ready.
entries.summary: When you come back after a while, Saka now gets a short labelled recap of your last messages so the conversation continues instead of restarting. Report PDF links also wait ten seconds after upload so the file is ready before you tap. Signup now reads "Meet your car's new friend", and the changelog is a quick preview — no read-more.

entries.title: A little more fire
entries.preview: Ember-orange buttons and glows, a burning headline word, and a brand-new drawer menu.
entries.summary: The site picks up a hot signal colour: fluorescent ember orange on the primary buttons, the most-popular plan and small sparks like focus rings and the FAQ marker — always with dark, high-contrast text. On tablet and mobile a new burger opens a full-screen drawer menu whose links rise into place over a glowing navy backdrop.

entries.title: The banner that follows you
entries.preview: The launch banner now sticks while you scroll — and duplicate signups stop before Continue.
entries.summary: The launch offer banner now stays visible as you scroll on every screen size, with a soft glow, a live slots counter and a mobile layout that centres everything. The signup form also checks your number and email live as you type: if either already has a Saka account you are told straight away, and the Continue button stays greyed out until both are free.

entries.title: The launch offer, up front
entries.preview: A live banner with slots left — and a tick box to opt out of the 365-day offer.
entries.summary: The website now shows the launch offer in a slim banner with a live slots-left counter and a note that your use helps us polish Saka for production. The signup form carries a tick box (checked by default) for the first-50 365-day trial — uncheck it for the standard 30-day flow. The banner disappears automatically once the slots are gone.

entries.title: Saka, more human
entries.preview: Quick logs now get lightning confirmations; saves never end in a menu.
entries.summary: Persona v4: Saka mirrors your style - fire off a shorthand log and get a lightning confirmation of the key figures, or ask for a detailed breakdown and get clean bullets with precise labels. Confirmations never repeat twice in a row, a completed save never ends in a menu, your phone's country code now locks your country on day one, and every record can carry an optional label you can search.

entries.title: The first 50 get a whole year
entries.preview: The first 50 accounts that register their first car get 365 days, no card.
entries.summary: A launch thank-you: the first 50 accounts that register their first car get a full 365-day trial - every feature unlocked, no card, no catch. Once the first 50 are in, the normal 30-day welcome trial keeps running for everyone else.

entries.title: Your car's friend
entries.preview: Add a PSV, licence or insurance in one line - Saka saves it or asks one question.
entries.summary: Ask to add your PSV, licence or insurance and Saka saves it straight away — or asks one short question for the missing number or date, then remembers the rest. Owners no longer need an assigned driver for that. The website now speaks to one-car owners first, in plain words.

entries.title: One plan, one model
entries.preview: Your plan decides the model: paid and trial get Sonnet, free stays on Haiku.
entries.summary: Your plan now decides the model: paid and trial accounts get Sonnet on every turn, free accounts stay on fast Haiku - no more switching mid-conversation.

entries.title: No more loops
entries.preview: Straight plan answers, one-line relabels, and fixes that sweep their whole bug class.
entries.summary: Questions about your plan get straight answers, a draft can be relabelled in one line, short plate names work, and Saka stops messaging numbers that can never receive. Plus a new rule: every fix now sweeps the whole class of bug it belongs to.

entries.title: Support that reaches a human
entries.preview: Support opens a real ticket first, and part names show up in your records.
entries.summary: Support requests now open a real ticket before Saka says it forwarded them, a waiting support intake owns your next message, and statements mid-draft park the draft instead of looping. Part names and notes show up in your records.

entries.title: Trials that start on day one
entries.preview: Your welcome trial runs from the day your first asset is registered.
entries.summary: Your welcome trial now runs from the day your first asset is registered, upgrading never cuts it short, and the assistant answers plan, switch and driver-profile questions straight instead of looping.

entries.title: Trials that actually start
entries.summary: A rare database mismatch was stopping welcome trials from starting; it is fixed, every eligible account has been repaired, and the assistant now tells the truth about your plan instead of looping.

entries.title: No duplicate support tickets
entries.summary: Escalation emails that land back in the support inbox are no longer turned into duplicate tickets, so each conversation stays as one clean thread.

entries.title: Care that follows through
entries.summary: Every support message - on WhatsApp or by email - now becomes a tracked ticket with a lifecycle, a thread and an audit trail, and the care team can reply on both channels from one console.

entries.title: One support inbox
entries.summary: Support now lives at support@reports.sakafleet.com across the assistant and the website, replies from that inbox still reach you on WhatsApp, and escalations now land with the team by email and WhatsApp.

entries.title: Clearer document storage
entries.summary: Receipt and document storage is now spelled out in the terms and privacy pages: Saka reads every photo, the Free plan keeps just the numbers, paid plans keep the original file, and any receipt photo can be deleted from WhatsApp.

entries.title: Every machine you run
entries.summary: Saka now speaks to every asset, not just cars: trucks, bikes, boats, generators, excavators and EVs are front and centre, receipts can be deleted on request, and old documents and OCR telemetry are cleaned up on a schedule.

entries.title: One account, calmer alerts, real inbox
entries.summary: Signing up twice with the same number or email is now impossible and the owner is told, Sentinel flags friction for a human instead of offering fixes, and support@reports.sakafleet.com email lands in the app ready to tend.

entries.title: Calmer alerts, clearer start
entries.summary: Team alerts now flag only the fixes actually waiting for review, an unverified number that says "Huh?" gets a clear way forward instead of the same line, and every new account starts cleanly on Free with no stray trial dates.

entries.title: One step at a time
entries.summary: Brand-new owners get exactly one next step: your first vehicle. Saka no longer asks for a driver licence before you even have a car on file.

entries.title: A warmer hello
entries.summary: Already set up on the website? Say hi and Saka goes straight to your first vehicle instead of welcoming you again — and the greeting now follows the language you actually chose.

entries.title: Saka answers for itself
entries.summary: The admin command list documents itself, and support now runs end-to-end: a request becomes a ticket, high-priority ones ping the team instantly, and an emailed reply lands back on the customer's WhatsApp.

entries.title: Clean starts, every time
entries.summary: The account-reset tool now clears every trace of an account (even chats saved in a different number format), so a fresh sign-up truly starts clean.

entries.title: Always up to date
entries.summary: Pushes now deploy automatically, a superadmin can reset an account safely with an emailed code, and new users get a friendly nudge to set up their first vehicle.

entries.title: Saves you can trust
entries.summary: Saka only says saved when it really saved, switching vehicles works even mid-log, and Stop now pauses politely instead of going quiet.

entries.title: Saka hears what you mean
entries.summary: Logging a repair as a sentence now actually saves it, asking for your fuel records shows them, and with two cars Saka asks which one before totalling.

entries.title: Sentinel looks deeper
entries.summary: Twice a week Saka's background supervisor audits the system itself and files a reviewable fix proposal for anything it finds — nothing changes without your say-so.

entries.title: Polished, reliable, everywhere
entries.summary: Messages read cleanly again, a mid-turn hiccup never leaves you in silence, and your fleet auto-audit now uses your own currency and Nairobi time.

entries.title: The right vehicle, every time
entries.summary: Editing your ledger now stays scoped to one vehicle, and one-line logs route by plate instead of guessing.

entries.title: Notes stay notes, fields stay fields
entries.summary: Saka no longer stores a note or label as the make/model, and saying make and model now edits the right field.

entries.title: Pick by number
entries.summary: The reminder menu is numbered now, so replying 3 picks the third option instead of looping.

entries.title: No more correction loops
entries.summary: Re-sending a correction during vehicle setup now just updates the field, and Sentinel tracks its own fixes as deployed.

entries.title: Add vehicles on trial, clear your chat
entries.summary: A trial now lets you add vehicles, the stray coupon message is gone, and you can clear the chat anytime.

entries.title: Learns per country
entries.summary: Saka keeps separate lessons and tone for each country, and the admin line can never be assigned as a driver.

entries.title: Fix tracking, simply
entries.summary: Marking a friction point fixed now takes the short id shown in the list.

entries.title: Nothing forgotten, nothing lost
entries.summary: Saka remembers your whole conversation, and every friction point is tracked from pending to fixed with a permanent log.

entries.title: When to replace your tyres? Just ask
entries.summary: Ask Saka "when should I replace my tyres?" and she answers from your own reminders — or offers to set one, without guessing.

entries.title: Just ask, in plain words
entries.summary: Admins can now ask "what's pending?" or "show me pending proposals" and get the fix list straight away — no special syntax needed.

entries.title: Complaints heard, answers that read right
entries.summary: Tell Saka "you deleted the wrong entry" and she treats it as feedback — not an edit. Empty searches now read in plain words too.

entries.title: Add a second car — and check its mileage
entries.summary: Already have a vehicle? Ask Saka to add another and registration just works. And "what's my current mileage?" now reads the vehicle's real odometer, not your spending.

entries.title: Saka learns from every missed beat
entries.summary: When a reply misses the mark, Saka now diagnoses why and files a fix for review — so the next conversation goes smoother.

entries.title: Saka remembers what you just told her
entries.summary: Even before you save, Saka keeps your in-progress details in view — so she never asks you to repeat yourself.

entries.title: Fixing your draft, not losing it
entries.summary: When you tell Saka a number on a draft is wrong, she now fixes that draft — instead of saying she couldn't find the entry.

entries.title: Patience that never runs out
entries.summary: If a step trips you up twice, Saka shows the easiest way to type it — and after that, a human is one word away.

entries.title: Saka speaks, never scripts — fully
entries.summary: Every reply is now written conversationally for you, and a new compliance harness keeps Saka warm, clear and patient for everyone.

entries.title: Documents that keep improving
entries.summary: Saka now learns where document reading struggles most — country by country — and sharpens those readers first.

entries.title: Receipts from anywhere
entries.summary: Saka now reads amounts, currencies and plates the way your country writes them — and double-checks anything she isn't sure about.

entries.title: Your whole record, one answer away
entries.summary: Saka now answers from your recent logs too — and for anything missing, she tells you the one step that fills it.

entries.title: Registration just works
entries.summary: Send your certificate and Saka reads the right plate, make and model — and corrections now actually fix the right field.

entries.title: Smarter change control
entries.summary: Sentinel now proposes changes under one clean registry, and you review every one together with us before anything ships.

entries.title: A warmer, clearer Saka
entries.summary: Short, plain sentences, one question at a time, and patience for everyone — whatever your age or tech comfort.

entries.title: Saka speaks, never scripts
entries.summary: Every reply is now written conversationally for you, in the moment — no more canned lines.

entries.title: Your data, always at hand
entries.summary: Ask Saka when your insurance or licence expires and she answers from your own records — every time.

entries.title: Logbooks register vehicles
entries.summary: Send your registration certificate and Saka reads the plate, make and model straight into registration — no more receipt mix-ups.

entries.title: One-tap quick edits
entries.summary: Saka can now offer quick-edit buttons for plates, entries and document dates — with the same replies when buttons aren't available.

entries.title: Smarter fixes & quieter alerts
entries.summary: Completeness complaints now get the full answer, and Cloud Run deploy noise stays out of your alerts.

entries.title: One signup, one place
entries.summary: Email verification now happens only on the website — WhatsApp registration no longer asks for email or a code.

entries.title: Reliable document reading
entries.summary: Sending a photo or PDF now always gets a reply, even if the document can't be fully read.

entries.title: Sign up first (documents too)
entries.summary: Unverified users are now guided to sign up before sending documents.

entries.title: Sign up first
entries.summary: New WhatsApp users now sign up on the website before chatting.

entries.title: Cleaner first hello
entries.summary: New WhatsApp users are now gently guided to sign up first, before adding a vehicle.

entries.title: Turn ideas into work
entries.summary: The superadmin can now turn a feature idea into a planned work item in one step.

entries.title: Smoother admin review
entries.summary: Reviewing feature ideas in the admin console now gives a clear, friendly answer.

entries.title: Short links live
entries.summary: Report PDF and checkout links now arrive as short, branded links.

entries.title: Your fixes and ideas, together
entries.summary: The superadmin now reviews pending fixes and upcoming feature ideas in one place, and brand-new WhatsApp chatters are gently pointed to the website to sign up.

entries.title: Two AI brains, one helper
entries.summary: Saka now routes everyday chats through a fast model and the trickier questions through a sharper one, so answers stay quick and clear.

entries.title: Sign up on the website
entries.summary: Vehicle setup now happens on sakafleet.com — Saka meets you on WhatsApp once your email is verified.

entries.title: Cleaner signup, your language
entries.summary: The signup form no longer asks you to start the chat - Saka messages you first, in your language. Local prices now show the USD amount as a small hint.

entries.title: Multi-record paragraphs
entries.summary: Paste a whole day of records in one message and Saka replies with a numbered plan card - 1 Save all, 2 Edit one, 3 Cancel. Every row is written and audited separately; no invented dates.

entries.title: Corrections 2.0
entries.summary: Ledger edits are now delete & re-log: the original entry date is kept, the old row is removed with a full audit snapshot, and restore can never duplicate a corrected row.

entries.title: Your records answer back
entries.summary: "How much did I spend on fuel last week?" is answered instantly from your ledger - sums, counts and averages, zero guesswork.

entries.title: Draft cards
entries.summary: Narrative logs confirm through a clean card - Vehicle, Type, Amount, Volume, Fill, Odometer, When, Place - with 1 Save / 2 Change / 3 Cancel.

entries.title: One sentence is a whole record
entries.summary: "Spent 5500 on diesel yesterday at Shell, 40L at 50350 km, full tank" is parsed deterministically into a ready-to-save log.

entries.title: Editable ledger
entries.summary: my entries → edit 2 / delete 2 → before/after diff and a 30-minute restore. Locked fields (VIN, plate, date) can never be changed.
